## Legal Moves

Treat a valid argument like a *legal move* in a game. 

Today we define the
moves: eight named rules, and two rules?


## Warm Up

A *valid argument* is a *legal inference*. 

- If the lab is open, I’ll go. The lab is open. **So I’ll go.** 

- If the exam is today, the forum is quiet. The forum isn’t quiet. **So the exam isn’t today.** 

---

## A Puzzle

Your friend \_\_\_\_\_\_\_ .

1. If BC has Chunkys, they go to BC.
2. If they go to BC, they miss the kitten.
3. They did not miss the kitten.
4. They went out today.
5. They only go out for Chunkys or for kittens.
6. Nobody goes out for a kitten unless they love kittens.

\

**Do they love kittens?**

::: notes
Ask before saying anything. The usual first answers are "they went for the
cookie" and "you cannot tell", and both are wrong for interesting reasons.

Nothing in the premises mentions how they FEEL until premise 6 -- everything
before it is about a cookie, and the conclusion is about affection.

Premise 6 is the bridge. Without it the argument gets you "they went out FOR
the kitten", which is a different proposition from "they love kittens" -- a
good place to say an atom means one thing all the way through. It is also the
same disguised conditional as lecture 4's "No song appears on the Hot 100
without reaching #1": two negation words hiding an implication.

Do not solve it now. Come back to it after the rule cards; by then they will
have the four rules it needs. The load-bearing premise is 2: it is what lets a
fact about a kitten rule out Chunkys, and it is the one nobody questions.
:::

## Rule Card: Modus Ponens [M.PON]

<div class="card rule">
From <code>p→q</code> and <code>p</code>, infer <code>________</code>.
</div>



**Ex:**  
If the bus is full, I’ll walk. The bus is full. **________**

\ 

\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_ &emsp; is a tautology

::: notes
Blank: q      Example: So I'll walk.
:::

---

## Rule Card: Modus Tollens [M.TOL]

<div class="card rule">
From <code>p→q</code> and <code>¬q</code>, infer <code>________</code>.
</div>

**Ex:**  
If office hours moved, Slack has an announcement. No announcement. **________**

\ 

\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_ &emsp; is a tautology

::: notes
Blank: ~p      Example: So they didn't move.
:::

---

## Rule Card: Transitivity [TRANS]

<div class="card rule">
From <code>p→q</code> and <code>q→r</code>, infer <code>________</code>.
</div>

**Ex:**  
If tidy then joins are simpler; if simpler joins then faster viz; **________**

\ 

\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_ &emsp; is a tautology

::: notes
Blank: p->r      Example: So tidy => faster viz.
:::

---

## Rule Card: Elimination [ELIM]

<div class="card rule">
From <code>p∨q</code> and <code>¬q</code>, infer <code>________</code>.
</div>

**Ex:**  
Dinner is sushi or tacos. Not tacos. **________**

\ 

\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_ &emsp; is a tautology

::: notes
Blank: p      Example: So sushi.
:::

---

## Rule Card: Conjunction [CONJ] / Specialization [SPEC]

<div class="two-col">
<div class="card rule">
<strong>CONJ</strong>: from <code>p, q</code> infer <code>________</code>
</div>

<div class="card rule">
<strong>SPEC</strong>: from <code>p∧q</code> infer <code>________</code>
</div>
</div>

\ 

\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_ &emsp; and &emsp; \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_ &emsp; are tautologies



::: notes
Blanks: CONJ p^q      SPEC p (or q)
:::

---

## Rule Card: Generalization [GEN]

<div class="card rule">
From <code>p</code> infer <code>________</code>.
</div>


**Ex:** I rode my scooter today, **________**

\ 

\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_ &emsp; is a tautology


::: notes
Blank: pvq      Example: So I either rode my scooter or I'm a unicorn.
:::

---

## Rule Card: Resolution [RES]

<div class="card rule">
From <code>p∨q</code> and <code>¬p∨r</code> infer <code>________</code>.
</div>

**Ex:**  
Either study or soccer; if study then library. **________**

\ 

\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_ &emsp; is a tautology

::: notes
Blank: qvr      Example: So soccer or library.
:::

---

## Rule Card: Proof by Cases [CASE]

<div class="card rule">
From <code>p→r</code> and <code>q→r</code> infer <code>________</code>.
</div>

**Ex:**  
If it's a weekday I take the bus; if it's raining I take the bus; **________**

\ 

\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_ &emsp; is a tautology


::: notes
Blank: (pvq)->r      Example: So if it's a weekday or raining, I take the bus.

Note both branches land on the SAME r. That is what makes the conclusion a
conditional rather than a disjunction.
:::

---

## Rule Card: Contradiction [CONTD]

<div class="card rule">
From <code>p→F</code> infer <code>________</code>.
</div>

**Ex:**  
If I'm free Friday, then 1 = 2. **________**

\ 

\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_ &emsp; is a tautology

::: notes
Blank: ~p      Example: So I'm not free Friday.

The one rule with a single premise and a constant in it. If assuming p forces
something false, p was false. Say only that much now -- Monday this becomes
proof by contradiction, and it is the reason CONTD is on the Sheet.
:::

---

## Fallacy Cards (flash)

<div class="two-col">
<div class="card rule">
<strong>Affirming the consequent</strong> ❌  
<code>from p→q, q infer p</code>
</div>
<div class="card rule">
<strong>Denying the antecedent</strong> ❌  
<code>from p→q, ¬p infer ¬q</code>
</div>
</div>

---

## Validity

**SPEC**: $(p\wedge q)\rightarrow p$ is this always true?


## INValidity

**Affirming Consequent**: $((p\rightarrow q)\wedge q)\rightarrow p$ is this always true?


| $p$ | $q$ | $p\rightarrow q$ | $(p\rightarrow q)\wedge q$ | $((p\rightarrow q)\wedge q)\rightarrow p$ |
|---|---|:--------:|:--------:|:--------:|
| F | F |       |      |      |      
| F | T |       |       |       |       
| T | F |       |       |       |       
| T | T |       |       |       |

## Micro Rule Cards {.smaller}

These are the ten on your **Formula Sheet**, in the Sheet's own names. Keep it
next to you. You will need them Monday.

:::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
- **M.PON**: from `p→q, p` infer `q`
- **M.TOL**: from `p→q, ¬q` infer `¬p`
- **TRANS**: from `p→q, q→r` infer `p→r`
- **ELIM**: from `p∨q, ¬q` infer `p`
- **CONJ**: from `p, q` infer `p∧q`
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
- **SPEC**: from `p∧q` infer `p` (or `q`)
- **GEN**: from `p` infer `p∨q` (any `q`)
- **RES**: from `p∨q, ¬p∨r` infer `q∨r`
- **CASE**: from `p→r, q→r` infer `(p∨q)→r`
- **CONTD**: from `p→F` infer `¬p`
:::
::::

**Common traps:**

:::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Affirming consequent: `p→q, q ∴ p` ❌
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
- Denying antecedent: `p→q, ¬p ∴ ¬q` ❌
:::
::::
